name: MemOS (MemTensor)
one_line: A Python 'memory operating system' (FastAPI server plus library) that stores LLM-extracted textual memories as nodes in a graph database, writes a fast raw window first and replaces it with LLM-extracted facts in a background scheduler, and also defines KV-cache (activation) and LoRA (parametric) memory types, the latter only as a placeholder.

locomo.protocol: OmniMemEval, MemOS cloud deployment; answer model gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14, judge gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18; cat 1-4 = 1,540 q (SH 841 / MH 282 / T 321 / OD 96); SH 92.51, MH 88.65, T 85.05, OD 69.79; average answer-stage context 5,400 tokens
locomo.source: MemTensor/OmniMemEval docs/user_memory/results.md lines 24-33, 71-101; MemOS README.md lines 59-79

locomo.protocol: T-Mem / HyperMem harness, gpt-4.1-mini builds memory, gpt-4o-mini reader and judge; deployment (cloud or OSS) not stated

arch.product.t: Three products share the name: (1) the open-source Python engine and FastAPI server (src/memos, routes under /product), (2) MemOS Cloud (hosted API, the source of the 88.83 figure), and (3) a separate TypeScript local plugin (apps/memos-local-plugin, SQLite, L1 trace / L2 policy / L3 world model / Skill) for OpenClaw, Hermes and DeepSeek Harness. This record traces (1) unless stated.

arch.truth.t: The graph database node store is the source of truth: every textual memory (fact, preference, tool, skill, raw file chunk) is a node with text, metadata and embedding. Raw turns are not kept as their own durable layer; the fast raw window is deleted once fine extraction succeeds, and only copies of source messages survive inside each derived node's metadata.sources.

arch.stores.t: Default server: Neo4j Community for nodes and edges plus Qdrant for vectors (neo4j-community backend wraps an external vec_db); alternatives Neo4j Enterprise, NebulaGraph, PolarDB, Postgres; Milvus for preference memory in the legacy MOS config; Redis optional for scheduler queues and status; SQLite or MySQL for user management.

arch.graphdb.t: Neo4j Community by default (GRAPH_DB_BACKEND / NEO4J_BACKEND = neo4j-community); PolarDB (Apache AGE style, 5,270 lines) is the largest backend and appears to be the cloud path. A merged PR on dev-v2.0.36 moves knowledge-node relationships into node metadata because a 'replacement graph backend' has no edges.

arch.scope.t: Memories are partitioned by cube: user_name = cube_id is a property filter on every graph query (shared DB) or a separate DB per user (use_multi_db). Requests carry readable_cube_ids / writable_cube_ids; several write cubes produce a CompositeCubeView. session_id is a soft priority signal on search, not a filter.

write.entry.t: POST /product/add (APIADDRequest: messages, user_id, writable_cube_ids, async_mode, custom_tags, info, is_feedback) -> AddHandler -> SingleCubeView.add_memories -> mem_reader.get_memory -> text_mem.add. Also the MOS Python API (MOS.add) and an MCP server.

write.receipt.t: Default async_mode='async': the call parses the messages into token windows, embeds them with no LLM call, writes them durably to the graph as 'mode:fast' nodes, then enqueues a mem_read task and returns. The queue is an in-process Python Queue unless MEMSCHEDULER_USE_REDIS_QUEUE=true, so queued fine extraction is lost on restart (the raw window survives). 'sync' + mode 'fine' extracts in the request.

write.roles.t: One extractor sees all roles; its prompt writes from the user's perspective, keeps assistant content only if the user acknowledged it, and lets the LLM label each item UserMemory or LongTermMemory. Preference extraction runs only on user-role sources (assistant/system/tool blocked). Tool calls go to a separate ToolTrajectoryMemory extractor gated on 'tool:' markers.

write.firewall.t: No prompt-injection or poisoning defence on the main fact path. A regex source filter strips recalled-memory blocks ('MemOS LONG-TERM MEMORY', <memories>), reasoning tags and runtime metadata, but only before preference extraction, as an echo guard. An optional LLM hallucination filter (SIMPLE_STRUCT_ADD_FILTER, off) exists only in the older SimpleStruct reader; add_before_search keep/drop is dead code.

write.governance.t: No PII redaction at write. Retention is capacity-based: per-type caps (code fallback WorkingMemory 20, LongTermMemory 1,500, UserMemory 480; server default 1e6) enforced by hard DETACH DELETE of the oldest nodes by updated_at once 80% full. Delete endpoints exist by memory id, file id, filter or session, plus record-level delete and recover.

segment.unit.t: A token window of one add call: messages are concatenated into windows of up to chat_window_max_tokens = 1,024 tokens with a 200-token overlap, and one fine-extraction call runs per window. Windows never span separate add calls.

segment.rule.t: Boundary is purely token count (1,024 per window, 200 overlap); items larger than the window are split by the configured chunker. There is no topic or time boundary detection. Per PR #2462 the 1,024 value is hard-coded and never passed from api/config.py.

segment.measured.t: Not found. Inferred: the bundled LoCoMo ingestion posts 2 messages per add call for each of two speaker perspectives, so about 5,882 add calls and about 5,882 windows for LoCoMo.

extract.calls.t: Per window in fine mode, 4 extractors run in parallel: string facts (1 LLM call), tool trajectory (LLM only if the window contains tool output), skill (only if a skills repository is configured), and preference (2 calls, explicit and implicit, only if ENABLE_PREFERENCE_MEMORY=true, default false). Default chat: about 1 LLM call per window.

extract.facts.t: The LLM returns a 'memory list' of {key, memory_type, value, tags}; each item becomes a node. The prompt asks for detailed, self-contained third-person statements and says 'prioritise completeness and fidelity over conciseness', so items are long, not atomic triples.

extract.episode.t: The same call returns a 120-200-word 'summary' of the window. It is not stored as its own node; it is copied into the 'background' field of every fact extracted from that window.

extract.dates.t: The prompt instructs converting relative time to absolute dates using the message timestamp, separating event time from message time and stating uncertainty. chat_time is injected into each message group.

extract.neighbours.t: Not in the default path: _get_maybe_merged_memory is a no-op stub ('TODO: delete this function') and _merge_memories_with_llm has no callers there. The neighbour-aware memory-version pipeline (memory_version_switch, default off) calls hook implementations that are not in the open-source tree.

extract.failure.t: If the extraction call throws, the window text is stored as one UserMemory item. If the whole fine transfer fails, the handler returns before deleting, so the fast raw window stays searchable. Documented gaps: malformed JSON silently became zero memories with a 200 response (PR #2457), and items between the embedder limit and 1,024 tokens were stored with no vector and never surfaced in search (PR #2462).

graph.entities.t: No entity extraction. Nodes carry an LLM 'key' (title) and 'tags'; the graph recall leg matches on exact key or 2 or more overlapping tags.

graph.resolution.t: Not found. The prompt asks the LLM to resolve pronouns and aliases into full names in the text, but no entity nodes or identity merge exist.

graph.edges.t: With MOS_ENABLE_REORGANIZE=true (default false), a background reorganiser adds CAUSE, CONDITION, RELATE and CONFLICT edges between memory nodes, plus FOLLOWS, INFERS (LLM-inferred fact nodes), AGGREGATE_TO and PARENT. Raw file chunks get PRECEDING/FOLLOWING/SUMMARY/MATERIAL edges, which PR #2479 is moving into node metadata.

graph.communities.t: Off by default (same reorganise flag). optimize_structure runs every 100 s per scope: MiniBatchKMeans partitioning into clusters of 10-20, LLM sub-clustering of large clusters, and an LLM summary parent node per cluster linked by PARENT edges, giving a topic > concept > fact tree.

time.fields.t: created_at and updated_at (ingest time, ISO) on the node; chat_time per source message; no event-time or valid-from/valid-to. The APISearchRequest.reference_time field is declared but never read. Archived versions carry timespec and memory_form only under the closed memory-version plugin.

time.update.t: Only with reorganise on: for each new node, top-5 neighbours above cosine 0.8 are LLM-judged contradictory, redundant or independent; a conflict is LLM-merged into a new node and both originals are archived, and if the merge fails the older node (by updated_at) is hard-deleted. The default path has no update logic; a user-feedback route (/product/feedback) can LLM-edit memories.

time.dedup.t: At write: none by default (redundancy merge only under reorganise). At read: exact-text dedup, or 'sim' (0.92 threshold), or 'mmr' (default, lambda 0.8, threshold 0.92) over a 3x over-fetched candidate set.

derive.session.t: No session-summary node. The per-window summary is stored as 'background' on each fact. Cluster summary parents exist only under reorganise. The 'AllSummaryMemory' search type maps to LongTermMemory plus UserMemory.

derive.profile.t: There is no consolidated profile document. Preference memory (explicit and implicit PreferenceMemory nodes from user-only sources) is off by default (ENABLE_PREFERENCE_MEMORY=false). When on, the top 6 preferences are searched alongside facts and injected as a separate pref_string block. PROFILE_MEMORY_RESERVED_TOP_K defaults to 0.

derive.entity.t: Not found (no entity nodes). The nearest equivalent is the LLM cluster-summary parent nodes under reorganise.

derive.background.t: The mem_scheduler (OptimizedScheduler, dispatcher with 30 workers, per-label handlers) runs mem_read (fine extraction), add, query / mem_update (re-search on each chat query and rewrite WorkingMemory), pref_add, mem_feedback, mem_organize and mem_dream. The reorganiser runs its own threads, and the beta Dream plugin (off) writes Context, InsightMemory and DreamDiary nodes.

derive.forget.t: No decay. Forgetting is FIFO by updated_at under per-type caps (hard delete), the fast raw window is deleted after fine extraction, and WorkingMemory is trimmed to 20. A 'usage' history is recorded on retrieval but not used for eviction.

index.embed.t: Code default: Ollama nomic-embed-text; the shipped .env.example uses universal_api with text-embedding-v4 (DashScope, 1,024 dims); configurable to OpenAI text-embedding-3-large or sentence-transformers.

index.lexical.t: Off by default: BM25 (rank_bm25, in-process) behind BM25_CALL, fulltext behind FULLTEXT_CALL / FAST_GRAPH (jieba-tokenised keys). Neo4j Community's search_by_fulltext is a TODO stub; PolarDB implements fulltext.

index.vector.t: Qdrant (external vec_db with payload indexes on user_name, memory_type and status) behind Neo4j Community, or native vectors in Neo4j Enterprise / PolarDB / Postgres; Milvus for preference memory in the legacy config.

read.rewrite.t: Fast mode (the default) does no rewriting. In fine mode, an LLM TaskGoalParser returns a rephrased query, keys, tags and extra 'memories' to embed; an optional VEC_COT_CALL splits the query into sub-queries.

read.analysis.t: Fast mode does only jieba tokenisation, and only when FAST_GRAPH is on. Fine mode does an LLM parse of goal type, keys, tags and internet_search intent. There is no temporal or category classifier.

read.legs.t: In parallel: WorkingMemory (all recent, up to top_k), LongTermMemory and UserMemory (each with graph key/tag recall, vector top_k x 2, plus optional BM25 and fulltext), internet (off), tool memory (top 6), skill memory (top 3) and preference memory (top 6). This is all one embedding of the raw query in fast mode.

read.temporal.t: Not found. reference_time is declared on the request but unused; the only time-aware filter is the caller's metadata filter (for example created_at gt). Temporal reasoning is left to the answer prompt using CreatedTime stamps.

read.traversal.t: neighbor_discovery (default false) expands RawFileMemory hits to PRECEDING/FOLLOWING chunk neighbours at 0.8 x relevance. There is no multi-hop traversal over fact edges in the default path.

rank.fusion.t: Union of legs deduplicated by node id (no RRF), then reranker scoring, sort and trim, then rerank_knowledge_mem keeping a 0.5 share for file memories.

rank.rerank.t: Code default MOS_RERANKER_BACKEND=http_bge (bge-reranker-v2-m3 over HTTP, strategy single_turn); the shipped .env.example switches to cosine_local (embedding cosine with topic/concept/fact level weights, no cross-encoder). API flag rerank=true by default.

rank.gate.t: The API drops memories whose relativity is below 0.45 (request field relativity, 0 disables). Fine mode adds an LLM recall_for_missing_memories check that triggers a second fast search when the enhanced set shrinks. There is no explicit abstain signal.

rank.agentic.t: FINE_STRATEGY env selects recreate (default when mode=fine), rewrite, deep_search or agentic_search (a deepsearch_agent loop). The default API mode is fast, so all of these are opt-in per request.

answer.shape.t: A numbered list of memory texts (the chat path's _format_mem_block prefixes each with CreatedTime and caps it at 1,600 chars) plus an optional preference block, placed into the system prompt via a {memories} placeholder; Outer (web) and Personal memories are kept in separate blocks.

answer.size.t: Vendor-measured: 5,400 answer-stage context tokens per LoCoMo question on MemOS Cloud (4,151 on LongMemEval, about 1,600 on BEAM). OSS defaults: top_k 10 text plus 6 pref plus 6 tool plus 3 skill; the bundled LoCoMo script uses top_k 20 for each of 2 speakers (up to 40 memories).

answer.prompt.t: The chat path uses get_cloud_chat_prompt(lang) with memories substituted. The LoCoMo eval prompt (ANSWER_PROMPT_MEMOS) tells the reader to treat the most recent memory as truth on conflict and to compute relative dates from memory timestamps.

eval.best.t: 88.83 overall (SH 92.51 / MH 88.65 / T 85.05 / OD 69.79) on MemOS Cloud, 1,540 questions, vendor-run. No published LoCoMo score for the open-source engine was found in the repo.

eval.outside.t: From our notes, not re-verified here: 75.80 on the T-Mem/HyperMem harness (gpt-4o-mini judge) and 63.60 on LoCoMo-Refined with a strict Qwen3-14B judge (1,382 revised q). Both are 13-25 points below the vendor figure.

eval.models.t: OmniMemEval: answer gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14, judge gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18, memory-service model gpt-4.1-mini where required. The in-repo script reads CHAT_MODEL from env and judges with EVAL_MODEL (default gpt-4o-mini), 3 judge runs, plus Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B similarity.

eval.rigour.t: Mixed. Good: cat 5 excluded, model versions pinned, context tokens reported for all 14 backends. Weak: vendor-run; the cloud system is not the OSS code; the in-repo script ingests each conversation twice (once per speaker as 'user'), so search sees both perspectives, which helps; the reader model is env-dependent; no confidence intervals for LoCoMo.

cost.write.t: Inferred for the bundled LoCoMo ingestion (2 messages per add, 2 perspectives): about 5,882 windows, so about 5.9K fine-extraction LLM calls, plus 2 per window (about 11.8K) if preference memory is on, plus embedding of every fast window and every extracted fact; reorganise (off) would add per-node conflict judgements and cluster summaries.

cost.read.t: Fast mode (default): 0 LLM calls, 1 query embedding, 1 reranker call (HTTP BGE or local cosine). Fine mode: 1 LLM goal-parse call, 1 batched recreate/rewrite enhancement call, 0-1 recall-for-missing call plus a second search; deep or agentic modes cost more.

cost.where.t: Hosted by default: OpenAI-compatible chat and extraction LLMs (gpt-4o-mini in code, qwen3-max in .env.example), hosted embedder and reranker; local options via Ollama, vLLM and HuggingFace. KV-cache memory needs a local HuggingFace or vLLM model.

trust.provenance.t: Each derived node keeps metadata.sources (role, chat_time, message_id, content of the source messages), file_ids, working_binding to the fast window it replaced, and merged_from on merges. There is no trust score or provenance class; a confidence field exists but is not set by the extractor. PR #2454 reports the full source message duplicated once per chunk.

trust.erasure.t: Hard delete by memory_ids, file_ids, filter or session (graph DETACH DELETE plus vector delete); soft delete and recover by record id under memory versioning. No cascade: copies of a message inside other nodes' sources, merged nodes and Dream insights are not traced back.

trust.auth.t: API-key auth (Authorization header, SHA-256 hashed keys in Postgres, master key) only when AUTH_ENABLED=true (default false); internal requests bypass it. A rate limiter exists, but PR #2432 reports it never recognised Bearer keys.

trust.sharing.t: Cube-level sharing: one request can read several readable_cube_ids and write several writable_cube_ids, with per-operation PermissionDict lists (internal). The cloud plugin advertises multi-agent memory sharing. There is no per-record visibility enforcement beyond the 'visibility' metadata field.

extras.t: GeneralMemCube aggregates text_mem, act_mem (KV cache), para_mem (LoRA) and pref_mem; nine registered memory backends (naive_text, general_text, tree_text, simple_tree_text, pref_text, simple_pref_text, kv_cache, vllm_kv_cache, lora).

Off by default (ENABLE_ACTIVATION_MEMORY=false). The scheduler concatenates current WorkingMemory into one 'retrieved memories' prompt, prefills it once into a HuggingFace DynamicCache (or preloads a vLLM prefix) and reuses it via past_key_values on later turns, rebuilding only when the composed text changes. It works only with local HF or vLLM chat models, not the hosted API path.
Placeholder only: load() is empty and dump() writes the bytes 'Placeholder'. No training or adapter loading exists.

On each chat query, a mem_update task extracts query keywords, re-searches long-term memory and replaces the 20-slot WorkingMemory with reranked candidates (pre-fetch for the next turn); this is also the trigger for KV-cache refresh.

Fine search sends the retrieved memories plus the query to an LLM that keeps only query-relevant memories, merges near-duplicates, resolves pronouns and relative dates, and returns cleaned statements (batched, with retries). This is a read-time context-compression step.

The raw window is embedded and searchable immediately (tag mode:fast, background marks it as directly built from raw input), then replaced by fine LLM memories in the background; the working_binding id links the two so the raw node is deleted on success.

ToolSchemaMemory and ToolTrajectoryMemory from tool calls; SkillMemory written to a skills repository (local or OSS); image, file and URL parsers (markitdown, vision LLM); RawFileMemory chunk nodes with neighbour links.

Opt-in via MEMOS_ENABLED_PLUGINS=dream: builds Context nodes from pending memories, forms motives, recalls related memories, writes at most one LLM insight per motive and a diary entry. Context nodes are merged into normal search. Signals are held in memory only.
/product/feedback (or add with is_feedback) runs an LLM judgement over retrieved memories and issues add/update operations, with keyword-replace shortcuts and versioned updates.

An MCP server exposes add, search and chat. A hook system (hookable add/search, SEARCH_MEMORY_RESULTS, SEARCH_CONTEXT_RENDER, MEMORY_ITEMS_AFTER_FINE_EXTRACT) lets plugins rewrite results; the memory-version hooks are referenced but not implemented in the OSS tree.

apps/memos-local-plugin: SQLite plus FTS5 plus vectors; Tier-1 skills (top 3), Tier-2 trace and episode (top 5), Tier-3 world model (top 2), fused by RRF plus MMR into an InjectionPacket with char-capped summaries and an LLM filter with an output token budget. Injection is timed to turn start, tool search, sub-agent start or repair, not every tool call.

token_economy.t: Vendor-measured 5,400 answer-stage tokens per LoCoMo question on Cloud (lower than Mem0 17,395, Hindsight 24,683 and Cognee 32,532, but higher than Zep 1,862 and mem9 1,597 in the same table). OSS mechanisms: (1) LLM-written self-contained memory statements instead of raw turns; (2) read-time 0.45 relevance gate, MMR dedup (lambda 0.8, 0.92 similarity) over 3x over-fetch, then top_k 10; (3) per-type quotas (pref 6, tool 6, skill 3) and 1,600-char caps per item in the chat block; (4) optional query-conditioned 'recreate' LLM pass that drops irrelevant memories and merges duplicates; (5) optional KV-cache prefill of WorkingMemory so the memory block is not re-encoded each turn (local models only); (6) remove_prompt_example flag to shrink the extraction prompt. The cloud OpenClaw plugin claims 72% lower token usage (no method stated).

speed.t: Write: async by default; the request path is parse, embed and batch-insert (5 nodes per batch, up to 8 threads), and the LLM extraction runs in the scheduler (dispatcher with 30 workers, mem_read batches with up to 8 threads, fine items with up to 30 threads, 4 extractors in parallel per window); optional Redis Streams queue for multi-process. Read: fast mode has no LLM call, and up to 7 legs run in a 5-worker pool, each with parallel graph, vector and BM25 sub-legs; timed_stage telemetry logs per-stage ms and estimated input tokens. No latency numbers were published in the repo or the OmniMemEval results doc.

keep: Fast-then-fine write: persist and embed the raw window synchronously (zero LLM), extract in the background and swap via a binding id, so recall works immediately and a failed extraction degrades to raw-window recall.
One extraction call per token window returns both detailed facts and a window summary, and the summary is attached to each fact as background (episode context for free).
Read-side token control as an explicit pipeline: relevance floor (0.45), then MMR dedup over a 3x over-fetch, then per-type quotas (facts 10 / pref 6 / tool 6 / skill 3), then per-item char caps.
Optional query-conditioned 'recreate' pass that compresses retrieved memories into fewer, disambiguated statements; a good fit for an opt-in fine mode.
Typed memory layers retrieved by parallel legs with separate top-k budgets (Working / LongTerm / User / Preference / Tool / Skill), plus a KV-cache prefill of a stable memory block for local models.
avoid: Capacity eviction by hard DETACH DELETE of the oldest updated_at nodes, with no decay, archive or lineage, and Cypher built by f-string interpolation of user_name (src/memos/graph_dbs/neo4j.py:210-222).

Silent write failures: malformed extraction JSON became zero memories with HTTP 200 (PR #2457), and over-limit items were stored without vectors and never surfaced in search (PR #2462); queued extraction lives in an in-process Queue by default.

Most structure is off by default (reorganise, conflict handling, graph edges, clusters, preferences, BM25, KV cache), and the neighbour-aware merge is a no-op stub, so the default OSS engine is a single-stage LLM-fact vector store; the 88.83 comes from a different (cloud) system.
No write-time firewall or trust signal: assistant content enters memory when the LLM thinks the user acknowledged it, and recalled-context stripping applies only to preference extraction.
in_progress: dev-v2.0.36 (6 commits ahead of main, 2026-10-10): PR #2479 merged 'Decouple knowledge memories from graph-edge relationships'; it stores summary/material and raw-file neighbour links as node metadata because the 'replacement graph backend' lacks edges, which signals a move away from Neo4j-style edges (gh api compare main...dev-v2.0.36; PR #2479).

Open fix PRs on the write path: #2462 (items between the embedder limit and 1,024 tokens stored without vectors), #2457 (malformed JSON yields an empty successful add), #2454 (sources duplicated once per chunk), #2432 (rate limiter ignores Bearer keys) (gh pr list, 2026-10-11).

Memory versioning (memory_version_switch, NLI or LLM relation judge via MEM_VERSION_RELATION_JUDGE_PROVIDER, archived versions with timespec/memory_form) is wired into the OSS code but its hook implementations are not in the public tree (src/memos/mem_reader/multi_modal_struct.py:659-684; src/memos/api/config.py:787-788).
The Dream plugin is beta: signal store in memory, simple pending-count trigger; update/merge/archive write-back listed as future work (src/memos/dream/README.md).

Most recent main commits (2026-09-16 to 09-22) are local-plugin hardening: L2/L3 evolution, bounded L3 clusters, skill verifier retries (gh api commits; branches fix-20260921-local-plugin, release/memos-local-plugin-v2.0.13-beta.2).
